title: Layla and the River That Argued
logline: Layla fights Wahhaj until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Layla, who carried young Beiruti oud player, ran headlong against Wahhaj, who was one who observes, watches. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Layla noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Layla had fought so hard in Wahhaj was only the part of Layla that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
